summary: Mid-cycle invoice shows temporary overcharge due to credit timestamp mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Health reported a mid-cycle invoice (2026-03-09) showing a temporary overcharge: an interim negative line item followed by a compensating credit 10 minutes later. Customer noticed the overcharge on their accounting export and opened this ticket requesting clarification and an immediate provisional credit.

Impact:
- Customer reported a $7,412 provisional overcharge on 2026-03-09 invoice export.
- Nimbus flagged accounting hold on automated payments until clarified.
- Affects month-end reconciliation for the customer (enterprise / dedicated).

Environment:
- prod (us-east) dedicated capacity fallback to hosted routing for small time window
- Affected model: text-embed-512-v2

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1) Recreate large batch embed job used by Nimbus (job id redacted in attachment).
2) Force a regional postback replay in the postback-processor with out-of-order timestamps.
3) Observe metering service applying smoothing credits and then running a reflow that generates a negative interim line before final credit.

Expected behavior:
- Metering postbacks should be idempotent and credits applied exactly once; invoices should not show transient negative line items visible in customer's export.

Actual behavior:
- A transient negative line appeared on customer invoice export followed by a corrective credit; net final charge is correct but the temporary line triggered customer accounting alerts.

Logs / Evidence:
- Attached: postback-processor logs (postback-logs-654321.tar.gz), billing-export-csv-2026-03-09.csv, customer screenshot of accounting export.
- Postback stream shows three postbacks within a 12s window from two collectors; timestamps: 2026-03-09T14:23:01.120Z, 2026-03-09T14:23:00.925Z, 2026-03-09T14:23:13.403Z.

Customer request:
- Immediate provisional credit to offset displayed overcharge while we investigate.
- Clear explanation and permanent fix timeline.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Maya Thompson (Support): Acknowledged receipt. Escalating to Billing and SRE. Provisional credit request noted; raising SLA hold with Finance.
2026-03-10 | Nora Alvarez (Finance): Can confirm automated hold triggered. Placed provisional credit for $7,412 on 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. Will await engineering confirmation for final adjustment.

2026-03-10 | Ethan Park (SRE): Initial triage suggests out-of-order postbacks from regional aggregator caused the metering service to create an interim negative adjustment before final reconciliation. Collecting postback traces and correlation IDs.
2026-03-11 | Nimbus Health (Customer): Thank you — provisional credit applied. Please confirm timeline for root cause fix; our accounting needs assurance this won't recur.

2026-03-12 | Ethan Park (SRE): Confirmed a clock skew between collector A and collector B (~220ms) combined with non-idempotent postback handling in the smoothing window. Engineering PR to add strict idempotency keys and tighter ordering checks merged; rolling to prod 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 | Maya Thompson (Support): Notified customer of planned deploy and timeline. Finance to issue final invoice adjustment after deploy verification.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings: The postback-processor accepted three near-duplicate postbacks for the same batch due to collector clock skew and a gap in idempotency enforcement for smoothing credits. The metering pipeline applies a provisional smoothing adjustment immediately and later reflows when it receives the final ordering, which created a temporary negative line visible in the customer's invoice export. Root cause threads:
- collector clock drift (two collectors out of sync by ~220ms)
- postback-processor lacked a strong idempotency key scoped to (job_id, collector_instance, sequence) for smoothing adjustments
- invoice exporter surface shows provisional adjustments without collapse of transient states; downstream accounting export included the interim negative line.
Evidence referenced: postback trace IDs 2a7f9e.., 2a7fa1.., 2a7fb4..; billing worker logs at /var/log/billing/2026-03-09; perf snapshot of smoothing service.
Mitigation performed: Blocked collectors older than 150ms skew in aggregator and applied provisional credit immediately. Patch created to add idempotency keys and ordering window checks. Regression test added to ensure exporter collapses provisional adjustments before exposing to final invoice CSV.
resolution:
Temporary and permanent actions: 
1) Immediate provisional credit of $7,412 issued by Finance on 2026-03-10. Customer notified.
2) Engineering deployed fix to postback-processor (PR #182) 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC which: enforces idempotent smoothing adjustments, rejects out-of-order postbacks beyond 200ms window, and adds logging for postback dedup keys.
3) Billing team scheduled an automated invoice re-export and final adjustment to remove the transient negative line from customer's accounting export; finance will apply or reverse provisional credit accordingly on final invoice (expected 2026-03-13).
4) Follow-ups: SRE to monitor postback ordering metrics for 72 hours (until 2026-03-15). Customer success to confirm Nimbus Health's accounting reconciliation complete.
Status: provisional credit applied; fix deployed; final invoice adjustment pending verification.
final_resolution_notes: 2026-03-14: Finance reversed provisional credit and applied corrected invoice line after confirmation of stable postback ordering. Customer confirmed reconciliation complete and removed payment hold. Case closed with postmortem and monitoring playbook updated.
next_steps: SRE: Monitor postback-ordering-metric in us-east for 72 hours (alert if >0.5% out-of-order postbacks)
Billing: Run re-export and finalize invoice adjustment on 2026-03-13. Confirm with customer via CS.
Product: Consider export UX change to hide provisional adjustments until reconciliation completes
